text:
Jamie: CI red on master, intermittent failure in `scheduler/lockstep_test`. 3/10 runs failed on ubuntu-22 CI. Link: https://ci.internal/red/12345 :eyes:

ci-bot: Build 12345 failed: test timeout at scheduler/lockstep_test. Failing assertion at advance_clock() -> stacktrace snippet: `scheduler_test.go:214: expected event, got timeout`

Alex: Seen this pattern before. It times out in the simulated clock advance path. Can we rerun with serial jobs? `bazel test //runtime/scheduler:lockstep_test --test_arg=-run=Lockstep -j1`

Sarah: Can someone bisect? My hunch: retry-window change from last week might shift timings and expose race.

Jamie: Starting bisect now. Command I'm using: `git bisect start HEAD v2024.10 -- test/run_bisect.sh //runtime/scheduler:lockstep_test` — will post candidate commits.

Jamie: Quick update: bisect narrowed it down to 3 commits. Earliest suspicious commit: `runtime/scheduler: switch to system clock for RetryWindow` (sha: b7f3c2a).

Alex: Ah, switching to system/wall-clock would explain nondeterminism. Tests rely on monotonic/mock clock. Try forcing mock clock via env: `TEST_CLOCK=mock go test ./scheduler -run Lockstep -count 100`

Lena: Reproduced locally: `GOMAXPROCS=2 go test ./scheduler -run Lockstep -count 50` -> 1/50 failed with same stacktrace. Repro seed: 834912.

Alex: Good repro. Two action items: (1) short-term: quarantine or mark flaky in CI and add `-count` capture in failure output; (2) long-term: make scheduler tests use injected monotonic clock or deterministic tick driver. I'll draft a patch for the deterministic timer.

Jamie: Opening PR now to add repro steps + quarantine label and capture seed. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/p/r/3921 :pray:

infra-bot: CI rerun queued for build 12345 as requested by Jamie.

ci-bot: Rerun started: build 12345 (rerun #1). Will post status when complete.

Sarah: Thanks everyone. If rerun passes we'll still land the quarantine fix to avoid noisy master. If it flaps again we should fully quarantine and create an ENG-ISSUE to track replacing wall-clock usage. cc @eng-sre
